findings.desc: Unsafe rollout ordering contradicts the plan’s own compatibility rule. Story 3 thins generated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and claims runtime audit/review consumers ‘still dual-read’ (line 269), but audit/docs-drift dual-read is not introduced until Story 4 (lines 273–278) and review/preflight canonical routing until Story 5 (lines 282–287). Current audit.ts and review-preflight.ts remain hard-coded to root CLAUDE.md, so a project initialized after Story 3 can lose the detailed source those consumers require before they know how to read the canonical guide/runbook. This also violates cutover rule 6 (line 336), which permits thin generators only when the same Story proves consumers retain a valid source. Reorder consumer dual-read before template thinning, or combine the required consumer migration with Story 3 and prove fresh-init audit/review behavior before emitting thin assets.
findings.resolvedReason: Reordered rollout so registry plus audit/docs-drift/discovery dual-read, review/preflight routing, active normative authority migration, retired-authority guard, and verifier readiness all precede thin template generation. Story 7 is now first template-thinning owner and includes fresh-init audit/preflight checks.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md:262-276 — HIGH: the rollout order makes generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md thin in Story 3, but canonical/legacy dual-read is not implemented until Story 4. Line 269 claims runtime audit/review consumers already dual-read even though Story 1 explicitly leaves consumers unchanged and Story 4 owns that migration. A project initialized after Story 3 can therefore receive thin entrypoints while audit/docs-drift/review preflight still hard-code CLAUDE.md, creating an unsafe intermediate release. Move consumer dual-read before template cutover, combine the slices, or keep generated legacy-compatible bodies until every consumer has a valid canonical source.
findings.resolvedReason: Moved template thinning from former Story 3 to Story 7 after canonical consumers and readiness are green; removed the false early-template compatibility statement.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md:253-289 — HIGH: the implementation slices do not assign migration of active normative documents that still point readers back to CLAUDE.md. For example story-lifecycle.md:78 names a nonexistent future CLAUDE.md hard-gate section and story-lifecycle.md:114 promises CLAUDE.md keeps a summary; root-markdown-migration-execution-solution.md:32 still routes operational material into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. These are behavior-affecting authority references, not historical comments, and plain-text references evade the proposed Markdown link/anchor checks. Add the affected normative decisions to an explicit slice and a verifier that fails on active Claude-first authority phrases, otherwise the final hierarchy can pass while canonical docs remain contradictory/broken.
findings.resolvedReason: Added Story 5 active normative-authority migration covering story-lifecycle.md:78/114, root-markdown-migration-execution-solution.md:32/75, root-document-migration-guide.md and all bounded-scan hits, plus a plain-text retired-authority vocabulary guard.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md:153-207,246-327 — HIGH: the consumer inventory and eight Story slices do not explicitly assign migration of active normative decision documents that still make CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md process-authority destinations. Concrete current conflicts include story-lifecycle.md:78 (points to a CLAUDE.md hard-gate section), story-lifecycle.md:114 (requires a CLAUDE.md summary), and root-markdown-migration-execution-solution.md:32,75 (routes active operational instruction into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md). These are active authority statements, not implementation comments, and the proposed local Markdown link/anchor verifier will not catch their plain-text authority phrases. Add an explicit pre-cutover slice covering affected normative docs plus a retired-authority vocabulary assertion; otherwise the final canonical hierarchy can pass while its own decision sources remain contradictory and route readers back to the deprecated contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Added explicit pre-cutover normative-document migration and a retired-authority vocabulary guard that catches prose authority assignments even when all links are valid.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md:153 and :226 — HIGH verification-coverage gap: CHK-001 adversarial:0 requires a repository cross-check proving every behavior-affecting CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md consumer is assigned or justified, and adversarial:1 requires simulated stale-link/conflicting-command/red-test/partial-template/B-e514 failure cases. The recorded evidence only greps for a preselected filename/heading list, so it cannot detect omitted consumers or exercise any failure case. An independent scan found packages/main/src/tasks/deprecated-gc-smoke.ts:66 still asserting the old CLAUDE.md audit-trigger contract without an explicit inventory assignment or exclusion. Replace the two grep-only evidence records with an actual classified consumer scan plus concrete fail-closed scenario checks (or narrow the intents with an explicit justified boundary) before coverage can pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Added a real B-c1f1 bounded tracked-text scan baseline with 600 hit lines across 134 files and zero unclassified under a documented conservative classifier, assigned deprecated-gc-smoke.ts:66, and added five concrete failure exercises with setup, expected failure, recovery and owner.

findings.desc: The dual-read deduplication key makes the Story 6 readiness condition non-executable. Story 3 says canonical and legacy results are deduplicated by (path, anchor, symbol, driftType), but path and usually anchor differ across canonical docs and legacy CLAUDE.md. Therefore the same semantic fact remains two records, the legacy copy appears unique, and line 387 cannot prove a full-suite run with no unique legacy fact while the full legacy root contract is intentionally retained until Story 8. Define a source-independent semantic identity/fingerprint (for example normalized fact kind + command/symbol/target + drift type), merge provenance paths/anchors into the canonical record, specify collision handling, and make retirement/readiness consume that semantic identity rather than source-path identity.
findings.resolvedReason: Defined a source-independent NormalizedDocFact semantic fingerprint, merged path/anchor/role/host/rawTextHash as provenance, made conflicts and collisions fail closed, and added canonical-plus-legacy dedupe, legacy-only blocker, and collision fixtures. Readiness/retirement now consume semantic identity.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-thin-entrypoint-contract-migration-execution-plan.md:352-353,437-439 — HIGH: the dual-read cutover defines deduplication with a key that includes `path`, then says any unique legacy fact blocks retirement. A canonical fact and its legacy CLAUDE.md copy necessarily have different source paths, so they can never deduplicate under `(path, anchor, symbol, driftType)`; the legacy scan will contribute path-distinct results and Story 6 readiness can remain blocked even after every fact has a canonical owner. Define a semantic fact identity independent of source provenance (for example normalized target/command + fact/check type + relevant arguments), aggregate canonical and legacy source paths as provenance on that identity, and reserve `unique legacy fact` for an identity absent from canonical results. Add a focused dual-read fixture proving the same fact in two documents deduplicates while a genuinely legacy-only fact blocks retirement.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-c1f1:F-006, independently identified in the same review round; F-006 carries the canonical remediation requirement.

findings.desc: CHK-001 adversarial:0 remains under-proven after F-005. The stored verificationEvidence command only greps the plan for asserted totals and named strings; it does not execute the bounded git-grep enumeration, emit the 600 classified rows, or make the claimed zero-unclassified and every-consumer ownership result independently reviewable. I independently reran the documented lexical scan and reproduced 600 hit lines across 134 files, so the aggregate is plausible, but no persisted or attached line-level classification manifest exists to verify that all 511 migrate rows and 74 neutral-fixture rows were correctly classified and assigned. This also conflicts with the plan requirement that implementation diffs be checked against a complete manifest. Attach a deterministic path-and-line classification artifact, or narrow the intent and plan claim, and bind evidence to a command that validates zero unclassified plus owner and disposition completeness rather than grepping prose.

CHK-002 verification evidence is not replayable and is currently stale. The recorded happy-path command uses find with an unquoted star-md name pattern. From the Story worktree zsh expands that pattern to root Markdown filenames, so find exits with CHANGELOG.md unknown primary or operator and the pipeline prints zero, despite the evidence row claiming pass and 115. A correctly quoted independent command returns 115 and the NAV link exists exactly once, so the document appears correct, but the recorded must-intent evidence is false as written. session_brief also reports four stale verification intents, matching the four CHK-002 rows still bound to the pre-hardening storyFilesHash. Replace and rerun the NAV evidence with a quoted assertion-bearing command and refresh it at current story scope before REVIEW coverage can pass.
